speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether he can provide an update on the transition framework for carbon tax that was first introduced on 12 January 2022; (b) how does the transition framework for existing facilities in the emissions-intensive trade-exposed sectors ease the transition without eroding the price signal for such companies to invest in decarbonisation; and (c) whether an update can be provided on how much SMEs have drawn down on the Energy Efficiency Fund to build capabilities.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The first is, the Minister said earlier that EDB has been engaging affected companies.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I was just wondering how many companies have been reached by EDB and does he have an estimate about how many companies have not yet been engaged by EDB; and how many more to go, basically?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The second question is, is there any significant projected impact from the transition framework on Singapore's climate targets that arise from this, from the framework?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the first one, under this transition framework, EDB has been engaging the types of facilities in the EITE sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They are sectorally determined, so we have them in the chemicals, electronics and biomedical manufacturing sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The level of allowances, with EDB's involvement, will factor in the company's decarbonisation plans as well as benchmarking to internationally-recognised efficiency benchmarks, wherever it is applicable.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In time, when appropriate, the Government will release aggregated information on the amount of allowances provided.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But this is where I want to also sound a caution.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will need to bear in mind considerations, such as whether these disclosures will inadvertently divulge commercially-sensitive information.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think you can imagine that, in the energy and chemical sector, there are that number of players within Jurong Island and within the entire space.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: The second question is if there is a significant projected impact on the transition framework on Singapore's climate targets.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We want to spur and continue to nudge companies to decarbonise ahead of time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are mindful and we are very focused on achieving that target by 2050.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because this is a developing framework and the companies that we are engaging with are also looking at international benchmarks, in time to come, in about a year from now, I think, we will be able to give you a better, a clearer indication.
